newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Aug 15.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

As he began his tax reform campaign in earnest yesterday, Prime Minister John Howard vowed there would be big income tax cuts to lower and middle income earners, a tough crackdown on tax avoidance by the wealthy, and a closing of loopholes in the income and corporate tax systems. Page 1.

Federal Transport Minister John Sharp and Workplace Relations Minister Peter Reith have for the past year been working with key operators of union reform David Trebeck and industrial relations consultant Paul Houlihan on a secret plan to crack the power of the Maritime Union of Australia in preparation for the next time the union shuts down Australia's docks. Page 1.

Revised figures released yesterday by the Australian Bureau of Statistics indicate a drop in private sector wages in the three months to May, with full-time ordinary time earnings growing by just 0.3 per cent over that period, and by 3.5 per cent over 12 months. The figures have renewed speculation of another Reserve Bank interest rate cut. Page 3.

In plans revealed just weeks after its privatisation, the Melbourne Airport will offer discounts of up to 50 per cent on operating charges for airlines bringing in new business to Tullamarine. The move, aimed at increasing profitability and gaining additonal services, looks set to ignite a price war between Australia's major gateways. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A High Court ruling yesterday stated the former Labor Government unjustly took over mining leases held by gold miner Newcrest Mining at Coronation Hill in the Kakadu National Park when, in 1991, it extended the National Park to cover the Coronation Hill area. The decision could mean taxpayers will have to fork out millions of dollars in compensation to miners unable to mine in the World Heritage-listed area. Page 1.

While addressing a Liberal Party function in Brisbane last night, Prime Minister John Howard indicated middle Australia would benefit from his new tax reforms, and signalled that the reforms would protect State budgets through new revenue sources. Page 1.

Berlei announced this week it would relocate its operations from Lithgow in New South Wales to Asia. The move, which echoes similar moves in the textile, clothing and footwear industry because of reduced import tariffs, will leave 184 mostly female workes in the town without work. Page 1.

The High Court ruled yesterday that Telstra had breached copyright by playing artists' music to people on hold. The decision, applauded by the Australasian Performing Rights Association, sees Telstra faces multi-million dollar claims for royalties, and could increase prices for users of new communication services such as the Internet. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Prime Minister John Howard said last night his Government is committed to ensuring middle Australia pays "significantly less tax" as it moves to introduce tax reform. His comments followed a meeting yesterday of the Government's new tax task force which will prepare sweeping taxation reforms for Australia. Page 1.

Tariff cuts have forced the Berlei bra factory in Lithgow to relocate to Indonesia, leaving the mostly-female staff of 184 without jobs. The job losses follow the loss of about 1700 others in the town due to cuts in the power industry, the railways and the ammunitions factory, and mayor Gerard Martin has called on New South Wales Premier Bob Carr to consider Lithgow another Newcastle. Page 1.

In a decision yesterday that follows a 1987 incident in which a young girl was left brain-damaged after receiving an electric shock from an outdoor tap at her home, the High Court ruled landlords are liable for damages even if they are unaware of faults bcause they should inspect properties before tenants move in. Page 1.

Senior business figures in Sydney have supported a planned merger between the University of Sydney and the University of New South Wales' business schools. The merger would create a "super-school" which would concentrate on management and would have a stong presence in the expanding Asia Pacific education market. Page 1.
THE AGE

As Prime Minister John Howard pushed tax reform yesterday, economist Access Economics said a goods and services tax of about 15 per cent would be required to remove the wholesale sales tax, petrol taxes and payroll taxes, while the Federal Opposition said the changes Howard was planning would require a GST of about 25 per cent. Page 1.

Following the release of a damning report of the inquiry into last year's Black Hawk helicopter disaster that killed 18 servicemen, three officers will be charged with disciplinary offences, a move that is expected to cause some conflict within middle-ranking officers who feel the officers are scapegoats for the disaster. Page 1.

A study conducted by the Financial and Consumer Rights Council on the gambling habits of women has urged the Victorian Government to remove all gaming machines from shopping centres and retain the cap on machine numbers. The study said the easy location of such facilities made it easier for women to gamble. Page 1.

Master Builders Association of Victoria executive director Brain Welch said yesterday the State's building industry expects to stay in a decline until at least the end of the century following the boom created by the construction of Melbourne's Crown Casino. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
